s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy, erythematous to violaceous skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Multiple milia in the superficial dermis on histopathologic examination
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene identified by whole-exome sequencing
Sanger sequencing confirmed cosegregation of the variant

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: COL7A1 gene mutation and dermoepidermal separation

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation and chronic, progressive skin lesions

shortlist.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation and presence of milia

shortlist.label: Kindler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoepidermal separation, milia, and novel COL7A1 variant

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
shortlist.why_kept: Family history and genetic testing suggestive of epidermolysis bullosa

raw.rationale: The presence of a novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene, which is a common cause of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, along with the clinical features of progressive, itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques, dermoepidermal separation, and milia, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita
rejected.why: This is an autoimmune disease, and there is no mention of autoantibodies or an autoimmune process in the vignette.

rejected.label: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: This condition typically presents at birth or early infancy and involves the mucous membranes, which is not consistent with the patient's age and lack of mucous membrane involvement.

rejected.label: Kindler Syndrome
rejected.why: While Kindler Syndrome involves skin fragility and blistering, the specific genetic variant and histopathologic findings in this case are more consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.

rejected.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex
rejected.why: This condition typically involves mutations in the KRT5 or KRT14 genes, and the clinical features and genetic findings in this case are not consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex.
